text: A man asked me for coffee today after work and I politely told him no and then brought myself to McAllister's where I got this croissant, this roast chicken sandwich, and an entire bowl of broccoli cheddar soup and a Dr. Pepper for under $25. Now I'm not going to argue with you about how you like to date, just like I don't want you to argue with me about how I like to date, but coffee is never going to be an option for me. And just like I respect your choice of coffee, respect mine to not coffee. Look, guys, I already talked about this before. Having coffee or drinks on a first date is completely fine. It's casual, simple, and gives you time to actually talk. And if that's not good enough for her, fine, go find a girl who is happy to spend time with you, not with your wallet. But in this video, I want to focus on something else. How much more self-respect, self-love, and confidence women seem to have compared to many men today. I usually try not to openly judge women based on their looks. Everyone's taste is different and that's okay. But if we be honest here, the lady in this video is probably not a supermodel, yet her confidence is through the roof. And that's where men could learn something from women. Because I see so many guys who are successful for their age, educated, in decent shape, with solid prospects, and yet their confidence is close to zero. Maybe that's even you watching this video right now. And then you see a girl like that, rejecting a guy over coffee, and you think, how come she has higher standards than so many men out there? I'm not saying men should live in some delusion that they're the best just because they exist, but it's probably still better than walking around with no confidence at all. Ideally, your confidence should come from real progress. From working on yourself, improving your body, your career, your mindset. But you also need to accept and respect who you already are. Love the things you can't change and keep grinding on the things you can.
